# am_data_plane (Resource)

DataPlane Resource

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A data plane on its own MongoDB database. The configuration is write-only: AM never returns it.
resource "am_data_plane" "eu" {
  id          = "acme-eu"
  name        = "ACME EU data plane"
  type        = "mongodb"
  gateway_url = "https://gateway-eu.example.com"
  configuration = jsonencode({
    mongodb = {
      host   = "mongodb"
      port   = 27017
      dbname = "gravitee-am-eu"
    }
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `configuration` (String, Sensitive) Connection settings. Write-only: it can hold credentials. Parsed as JSON.
- `id` (String) Stable, immutable identifier for the data plane within its environment. Lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, starting and ending with an alphanumeric character. This is the value a domain's dataPlaneId refers to. Requires replacement if changed.
- `name` (String) Human-readable name of the data plane.
- `type` (String) Data plane plugin type identifier, matching the dataplane-am-<type> plugin. Immutable after creation. Requires replacement if changed.

### Optional

- `environment_id` (String) Identifier of the environment. Requires replacement if changed.
- `gateway_url` (String) Base URL of the gateway serving the domains bound to this data plane. Must be an absolute http(s) URL with a lowercase scheme; omitted or empty leaves it unset.
- `organization_id` (String) Identifier of the organization that owns the environment. Requires replacement if changed.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (ISO-8601 / RFC 3339, UTC). Read-only.
- `database` (String) Name of the database the configuration points at. Read-only.
- `hosts` (List of String) Hosts the configuration points at, as host:port. Read-only.
- `updated_at` (String) Last-update timestamp (ISO-8601 / RFC 3339, UTC). Read-only.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = am_data_plane.eu
  id = jsonencode({
    environment_id  = "DEFAULT"
    id              = "acme-eu"
    organization_id = "DEFAULT"
  })
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import am_data_plane.eu '{"environment_id": "DEFAULT", "id": "acme-eu", "organization_id": "DEFAULT"}'
```
